assessments.reasoning: The exact Commission URL rendered seven pages. Page 1 names v.1.1 twice. Article 1 on page 2 and Article 5 on page 3 contain the revised wording.

Recital 3 identifies v.1.1 as a revised licence adopted by the Commission. The sole article and annex expressly concern v.1.2. The decision supports the distinction between editions. [Decision (EU) 2017/863, pp. 1–2](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/custom-page/attachment/eupl_v1.2_en.pdf)
The pinned decision matches UUID 40943fe14c284ecc80c1f163fa75e959, display name, kind, edition scope, documentary revision and URL. The editorial state takes effect upon qualification.
The Index scope supports separate admission of identifiable historical licence editions and requires qualified evidence for canonical attributes. The editorial row supplies the specific values.

challenge.method: Checked for confusion with both adjacent editions. Compared the v.1.1 opening notice and Article 5 with v.1.0 and the v.1.2 annex. Checked the editorial UUID and the meaning of `active` against the pinned decision.
challenge.results: The later-version option in Article 5 distinguishes this rendering from v.1.0. The versioned opening notice distinguishes it from the v.1.2 annex, which also contains a later-version option. The matching editorial row is prospective. No material contradiction was found.

limitations: The browser exposed the English rendering. Original PDF byte identity remains unverified.
The statement and decision carry the qualification condition. The standalone value `active` cannot establish that the gates have passed.
Adoption chronology, equivalence of translations, redistribution, installation and work-specific grants are outside scope.
reasoning: The Interoperable Europe document identifies itself as EUPL v.1.1 in its title and opening notice. The Index decision assigns the matching prospective entity the display name European Union Public Licence v. 1.1, kind `license`, and state `active` upon qualification.
